epics.title: Canonical approved scope, constraints, and procedural asset baseline
epics.outcome: A traceable technical delivery outline that records the accepted Prism Break PoC scope, non-goals, constraints, Director decisions, and procedural asset strategy without expanding scope.
acceptanceCriteria: A single outline records the accepted desktop-web Chromium PoC, Phaser direction, eight levels, four power-ups, four hero tracks, three dynamic layers, approved options set, non-goals, no date/budget/hiring/release assumptions, and no cross-browser/mobile certification.
All supplied source indexes are represented by Epic 0 and mapped to at least one downstream outcome.

Asset strategy decision 97e69fd5-9f3c-4ad0-9d01-5e84073be0c6 revision 2 is reflected as reproducible code-native visual and audio generation with declared project-use rights and hash-bound provenance; older sprite or external track wording does not create a new external media requirement.
Specialist ownership is justified only for creative specification and review; implementation remains game-engineer work and validation remains game-quality-assurance work.

epics.title: First increment: Phaser runtime and local-persistence proof
epics.outcome: Resolve the most consequential implementation uncertainty before content production by proving the engine pin, Chromium startup, and local best-score persistence mechanism.
acceptanceCriteria: An engineer-owned dependency-pin-phaser outcome selects one exact Phaser version within the accepted engine direction and produces a restored lockfile and standalone assertion output on the assigned authorized branch.
A local persistence probe records Chromium latest stable reload behaviour for best score and fails when persistence is not restored; no account system, cloud save, or privacy bypass is introduced.
The validation candidate launches in Chromium latest stable with a minimal scene and no blocking startup error; no cross-browser or real-device certification is requested.
This increment is the first experiment or deliverable chosen to resolve engine/runtime and persistence uncertainty before the playable core loop.

epics.title: Controllable core arcade loop
epics.outcome: Deliver a playable controllable core loop that makes the Prism Break promise observable and provides state hooks for levels, FX, audio, options, and scoring.
acceptanceCriteria: A Chromium build implements mouse paddle, click launch, arrow-key paddle alternative, ball motion, wall/paddle/brick collisions, brick destruction, lives, score, minimal HUD, and immediate restart.
A full run is possible: launch, paddle, bounce, destroy bricks, lose ball, lose lives, restart; score and HUD do not compete with play-field readability.
Core interactions produce distinct feedback hooks that later FX and audio can drive without forcing required FX-off variants.

epics.title: Eight-level progression and four power-ups
epics.outcome: Make the short arcade session legible and progressive through eight distinct clearable levels and four readable power-ups without scope expansion.
acceptanceCriteria: Eight static levels are clearable in Chromium with distinct layouts and palettes, preserving indigo-to-gold progression and avoiding unreachable brick pockets or unfair power-up spawns.
Multiball, wide paddle, laser, and slow-time can be acquired, show readable active states and expiry, do not obscure primary ball or paddle, and support fair level completion.

Power-up introduction order, drop rules, durations, strengths, and tuning are documented as delegated specialist design outputs and validated in an integrated build rather than treated as planning blockers.
No moving bricks, hazards, extra brick variants, procedural level generation, or other scope expansions are included.

epics.title: Procedural presentation, approved options, and accessibility evidence
epics.outcome: Deliver bounded high-juice presentation, the exact approved option set, and colour-safety/readability evidence without adding option scope or certification work.
acceptanceCriteria: Procedural visual presentation implements particles, screen shake, hit-stop, glow, chromatic aberration, and combined CRT scanline/vignette treatment at bounded high-juice defaults; optional particle intensity/density is not an acceptance requirement.
Pause/options exposes only the approved controls: global FX toggle, screen-shake intensity slider, CRT treatment toggle combining scanlines and vignette, and chromatic aberration toggle.
Global FX preserves legibility and necessary audio/visual cues; CRT and chromatic aberration allow selective reduction when global FX is enabled.
Representative gameplay captures during multiball, laser, slow-time, high multiplier, cluster destruction, and level clear show primary ball and paddle silhouettes remain legible.

Colour-safe evidence uses documented simulation or review plus representative captures reviewed by the responsible visual/accessibility lead and accepted by the game-director; formal accessibility certification is not required.

epics.title: Procedural hero chiptune and dynamic layers
epics.outcome: Make music a co-star through four final-quality original hero chiptune tracks and three reactive dynamic layers implemented with the approved procedural asset strategy.
acceptanceCriteria: Four original hero chiptune tracks are implemented through reproducible code-native procedural audio with declared project-use rights and hash-bound provenance; placeholder or temporary audio is not accepted as the final deliverable.
Three dynamic layers for rally, danger, and victory are implemented and triggered by gameplay state, rally escalation, threat, or level clear while remaining balanced against SFX.
Important audio cues are duplicated through visible multiplier, danger, power-up, or level-transition presentation so accessibility does not depend only on audio.

Playable Chromium playback is reviewed against the accepted quality bar; if procedural audio cannot meet the accepted quality, the evidence is recorded for game-director decision rather than silently reducing scope.

epics.title: Acceptance evidence and post-acceptance planning outputs
epics.outcome: Produce a coherent PoC evidence pack and post-acceptance planning outputs while preserving hypotheses, budgets, and forecasts as planning evidence rather than commitments.
acceptanceCriteria: An acceptance evidence pack is assembled from an integrated Chromium candidate: gameplay captures, build notes, option screenshots, colour-safety review, audio review, design review notes, and performance/readability notes.
Representative normal desktop Chromium gameplay is observed to remain stable and readable; 60 fps is treated as a target, not a hard measured gate unless instability is observed.
H1, H2, and H3 are treated as optional non-blocking planning hypotheses; any captured notes come from a playable build and do not add required variants or instrumentation scope.

Post-acceptance planning outputs—forecast, dependency map, and staffing proposal—are produced as planning artifacts, including audio/asset resourcing evaluation; no hiring, spending, or release authority is implied.

feasibilityFindings: The largest near-term feasibility uncertainty is the exact Phaser package version and persistence mechanism; Epic 1 is the smallest first increment that resolves both without detailing content production.

Procedural visual and audio generation is an asset-production strategy, not permission to lower accepted content or quality; evidence must show code-native assets meet the same originality, readability, dynamic-layer, and licensing expectations.
No external date, budget, hiring, release, cross-browser, mobile, certification, or test-variant scope is treated as approved.
technicalConstraints: Desktop-web Chromium latest stable verification only.
Phaser remains the accepted engine direction; exact version selection and lockfile ownership are engineering prerequisites.
Procedural assets require declared project-use rights and hash-bound provenance.
Only the approved option controls are implemented: global FX, screen-shake intensity slider, CRT treatment combining scanlines and vignette, and chromatic aberration toggle.
H1-H3 are optional non-blocking planning hypotheses, not PoC acceptance gates.
60 fps is a target, not a hard measured frame-rate gate unless instability is observed.
openFeasibilityDecisions: If code-native procedural audio evidence shows it cannot meet the accepted final-quality original hero-track quality bar, the Director must decide whether to accept a documented procedural quality compromise, authorize composer/hybrid resourcing, or amend audio scope.
